verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Dewas for now; lend only to profitable, low-concentration API units with clean compliance and tight monthly reporting.
title: Dewas Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**An API or formulation unit in Dewas buys solvents, intermediates and catalysts, runs multi-step chemical synthesis through reactors, and sells to formulators or exports.** Cash is made on yield and purity per batch, not on volume alone. **Value sits in the customer qualification and regulatory file, not the plant.** So when a proposal lands, check who has approved the site and for which market; if the buyer list is one or two names, ask for the supply agreement and the notice period.

## Where cash actually sits
**Working capital is the business: long receivables and high inventory holding are structural in this industry [10].** Peers show the same shape — one mid-size player ran working capital intensity of 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 [10]. **Capex is lumpy and compliance-driven; a single effluent or reactor upgrade can absorb a year of accruals.** So when a proposal lands, check the receivables cycle and inventory days against the peer range; if receivables stretch beyond the customer's own credit terms, ask for the ageing and the top-five debtor list.

## What has changed now
**The local signal is weak: Madhya Pradesh GST collections fell 0.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, 6.2 pp slower [D].** India-wide output is down 2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is up 21.6% YoY, a 23.7 pp gap [D] — money is chasing slower output. **Peer results are strong but not local: Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth [5].** Dewas-specific news is thin — only recruitment and topic pages [1][2][3] — so lean on first principles and peers here. **Rating reports are undated and old; treat them as shape, not current fact [8][9][10].**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue API and CDMO units with a diversified buyer base, own effluent treatment, and a product mix that is not one molecule.** The API industry grew at 8.4% CAGR between CY2017 and CY2022E and is expected at ~7% [11]; China still supplies 65-70% of India's API imports [11], which is the substitution opportunity. **Avoid single-customer contract research units and any borrower whose revenue depends on US clients alone — one such company's FY2024 revenue of Rs. 61.0 crore was hit by weak contract research demand [8].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure as working-capital-led: cash credit against receivables and inventory, term loan only for verified compliance capex.** Take monthly stock and debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and the effluent consent renewal date.
